_what: Committed sampling parameters for the AQ4 benchmark population (contract §21). Packet 2 owns cohort 4's seed. Cohort 5's seed is NOT here and is NOT chosen — §22 steps 1-2 belong to packet 3.
_law: These values are the commitment. Changing one changes the pre-registered population, so it is a Captain-visible act and not an edit: regenerate, re-hash, and say in the commit which number moved and why.

prng.algorithm: SHA-256 keyed ordering — sorted(pool, key=lambda oid: (sha256(label + NUL + oid).hexdigest(), oid))
prng.why_not_random_Random: A stateful PRNG reproduces only against a matching library. Cohort 4 must regenerate byte-identically at packet 9, months and possibly a Python version later, or §22 step 6 (audit the sampling procedure against the committed script) cannot pass. SHA-256 has no library-version surface.
prng.tie_break: oracle_id, so the order is total even under a hash collision
prng.domain_separation: every draw is keyed with its own label, so two classes drawing from the same pool cannot select the same cards by construction

ordering.never: dict insertion order, filesystem order, or card-name order — name order is a recorded defect (Tier 3's shipped top-10 is an alphabetical slice of a score tie, and A- Alchemy rows sort first)

cohort_4.seed_sha256: committed in population-manifest.json alongside the selection hash
cohort_4.per_stratum_rule: MINIMAL COMPLETE COVERAGE — one card per non-empty stratum. §21 pre-registers the stratification (delivery token × action family) and supplies no size, so the only draw rule with ZERO free parameters is one-per-cell. Any other rule (a fixed total, a size floor, proportional allocation) introduces a number the contract does not supply, and §10 of the packet directive forbids smuggling a population-size choice through implementation.
cohort_4.short_stratum_behavior: a stratum smaller than per_stratum yields everything it has and is REPORTED as short. Never merged into a neighbour, never dropped — collapsing a rare cell would silently change the pre-registered population.

stratum_definition.delivery_token: the FIRST delivery token in printed order from foundry_shape_extractor.deliveries_for_lines (grammar §2 ratified table, including §2's any-/other- scope facet). null when the card emits none.
stratum_definition.action_family: the FIRST CR 701 keyword action in PREDICATE position, printed order, using packet 1's cr701_keyword_actions (parsed from the CR at run time) and packet 1's effect-head boundary test. null when the card prints none.
stratum_definition.null_is_not_vocabulary: null is a JSON null and renders as (none). It is the absence of a value, not a coined stratum label.

cohort_6.split_rule: SHA-256 keyed order per family with label 'aq4-c6-split\u0000<class_id>'; even index -> OPEN half, odd index -> reserved for the holdout draw. Pre-registered, deterministic, and independent of any holdout seed, so publishing the open half exposes nothing about the holdout.
cohort_6.blind_half: never materialized and never printed by any packet-2 command
cohort_6.ramp_family_split: RAMP is ONE §21 family with three derived components, so its split is taken ONCE over the family UNION with label 'aq4-c6-split\u0000c6.ramp' — not once per component. Three independent splits would let one card be OPEN in one component and RESERVED in another; that is not a leak (packet 3 excludes development before it draws) but it leaves no single answer to 'is this card reserved?'. Each component then takes its open_half_cap exemplars from INSIDE the family's open half, so every arm stays visible: a single draw over a union this lopsided could return eight nonland mana sources and show a reader no land ramp at all.
cohort_6.ramp_is_benchmark_only: Captain ruled ramp a BENCHMARK family. No production ramp vocabulary is minted, no token is emitted, and no codebook axis is created. The components are named c6.ramp-* and exist only in this directory.

structural_classes.k_rule: Six exemplars per derived structural class. More than one so no single odd card can define a class (the 'did a named exemplar become the cohort?' failure); small enough that the open cohorts stay hand-adjudicable at packet 3.
structural_classes.min_class_rule: a derived class with fewer qualifying members than this is a named exemplar with a derivation written around it; the builder HALTS rather than publishing one as structure. Classes declared named_historical are exempt and labeled.

candidate_universe.gate_unchanged: the benchmark does not alter corpus membership; Gate #0's Commander arm applies here exactly as in every other foundry stage
candidate_universe.exclusion: Alchemy (A-) rows whose paper twin is present, implementing the ratified 'paper rows preferred over A- variants in sampling, resolution, and emit'
candidate_universe.exclusion_is_a_preference: a twinless A- row would be KEPT; the count of each is reported rather than assumed
candidate_universe.duplicate_prevention: oracle_id is the only card key and the universe is a dict keyed on it, so a duplicate is structurally impossible; the draw reports duplicate_ids anyway rather than trusting that

cross_cohort_overlap.policy: OPEN cohorts may overlap. A card can structurally qualify as several kinds of adversary at once and forcing exclusivity would misrepresent it; membership is metadata and the overlap matrix is published.
cross_cohort_overlap.hard_rule: holdout ∩ development MUST be empty. Enforced at DRAW time by draw_generic(exclude=...) — a check after the fact can only report a leak it cannot undo — and asserted by assert_disjoint_from_development.
